## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)

getwd()

data <- read_excel("lrc_attnd_for_R.xlsx")
View(data)
table(data[[1]])

# create participation buckets from the "to March 19" column
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    participation_bucket = case_when(
      `to March 19` >= 0  & `to March 19` <= 3  ~ "F (0-3)",
      `to March 19` >= 4  & `to March 19` <= 6  ~ "D (4-6)",
      `to March 19` >= 7  & `to March 19` <= 9  ~ "C (7-9)",
      `to March 19` >= 10 & `to March 19` <= 12 ~ "B- (10-12)",
      `to March 19` >= 13 & `to March 19` <= 18 ~ "B/B+ (13-18)",
      `to March 19` >= 19 & `to March 19` <= 20 ~ "A- (19-20)",
      `to March 19` == 21 ~ "A (21)",
      `to March 19` == 22 ~ "A+ (22)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# make a table of how many students fall in each bucket
bucket_table <- data %>%
  count(participation_bucket) %>%
  mutate(
    participation_bucket = factor(
      participation_bucket,
      levels = c(
        "F (0-3)",
        "D (4-6)",
        "C (7-9)",
        "B- (10-12)",
        "B/B+ (13-18)",
        "A- (19-20)",
        "A (21)",
        "A+ (22)"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(participation_bucket)

bucket_table

buckets <- cut(
  attnd$`to March 19`,
  breaks = c(-0.1, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 22),
  labels = c("0-3", "4-6", "7-9", "10-12", "13-15", "16-18", "19-21", "22"),
  right = TRUE
)

table(buckets)

#whomst


data %>%
  group_by(participation_bucket) %>%
  summarise(
    students = paste(`First`, collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

data %>%
  arrange(participation_bucket) %>%
  select(participation_bucket, `First`)

student_lists <- split(data$`First`, data$participation_bucket)

student_lists

student_lists[["F (0-3)"]]

install.packages("write_xlsx")
library(writexl)

output <- data %>%
  arrange(participation_bucket) %>%
  select(`First`, participation_bucket)

write_xlsx(output, "participation_by_bucket.xlsx")

1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
